overview: White builds a huge pawn centre with c4, d4, e5 and f4; Black attacks it with ...dxe5 fxe5 Nc6 and ...Bf5 or ...Bg4, aiming at d4 and e5. White needs to hold the centre while developing, otherwise it collapses. A sharp, forcing and theory-laden line in which White has space and Black counterattacks.

white_ideas.idea: Hold the broad centre with Nc3, Be3, Nf3 and Be2, then use space for a kingside initiative.
Push d5 or e6 when the moment is right, ahead of Black's development.

black_ideas.idea: Strike at d4 and e5 with ...dxe5, ...Nc6, ...Bf5 and ...Qd7, ...O-O-O.
Exploit overextension: if White's centre falls Black is better.

typical_structures.structure: White centre pawns on c4, d4, e5 against Black's piece pressure, with ...e6/...Bf5 and ...Nb6.

character.notes: Unbalanced and double-edged; the centre either holds or collapses, with forcing tactics.

soundness.notes: Sound though risky for both; used by strong players.

structure.notes: A large central pawn mass under tension rather than a locked chain.

approach.notes: A well-known main-line attacking try against the Alekhine.

level.notes: Forcing lines and a hard-to-judge centre; a standard 4.c4 line is intermediate.

character.reason: Forcing, tactical, and one inaccuracy can lose the centre.

structure.reason: White centre is under tension and not locked.

level.reason: Needs knowledge of forcing lines but the plans are clear.

plans.reason: White space against Black's hypermodern counterplay.
